## TL;DR

Healthy running-task cards now show their state without the repetitive “active N ago” suffix. The same recent-activity detail remains available through the shared styled tooltip on the task hint and pipeline state label. Silent and stuck states keep their inline recency signal. The review’s reported PipelineCard merge conflict was cleared by merging the current `main` into this task branch; RepoOS now reports that the branch merges cleanly.

## Work and rationale

This task changes the board’s status presentation in two places. In the task card, the shared active-engineer state continues to decide whether a task is coding, stuck, or in another state. For the healthy coding case, `TaskCard.vue` adds last-activity text as tooltip content while leaving the visible state label concise. Existing stuck and silent copy is retained, since that age is useful when progress has stopped. The tooltip uses the established `data-tip` mechanism and carries the required touch behavior, so users can discover the detail with hover, keyboard focus, or touch without a native browser title.

Pipeline cards follow the same information hierarchy. A healthy `ok` row omits elapsed time from the visible row and exposes state duration on its step label through the shared tooltip. Non-healthy states retain their elapsed text. This keeps the running board and pipeline views consistent while preserving the stronger “something is quiet” signal.

The implementation extracts formatting into `card-activity-recency.ts` so tooltip copy and timestamp handling are shared and testable. Existing tooltip behavior was extended to support touch reveal while avoiding accidental activation of the underlying task or agent action. The tests cover concise coding labels, tooltip content, touch interaction, preserved stuck/silent line copy, pipeline elapsed hiding and retention, and the formatting helper. The board shot fixture and declared review captures describe the intended board and pipeline states.

The latest review listed a conflict in `PipelineCard.vue`. I checked RepoOS landability and the branch’s merge preview, then merged the current `main` ref into this branch. The merge completed cleanly and changed only task bookkeeping files; RepoOS subsequently reports “Merge with main” as passed. The PipelineCard implementation itself therefore needed no conflict-marker or behavior rewrite.

## Approaches tried

I first inspected the task’s latest review report and current branch diff to determine whether the conflict was present in the worktree or only in the landing check. The worktree was clean, and `git merge-tree` showed that the current local `main` ref could combine with the branch’s PipelineCard changes. I then performed the merge so ancestry and integration state are concrete rather than relying on that preview. The merge completed with the automatic `ort` strategy.

For interaction, the implementation reuses the app’s shared `data-tip` system rather than introducing a card-specific popup implementation. This retains its established styled appearance and focus handling. The touch path opts into the shared tooltip’s short-tap behavior for these status hints, which preserves a way to reveal details on touch screens while the longer gesture remains available. Task cards still use their normal click action when the tooltip is not being revealed.

## Challenges and blockers

The review’s conflict report was stale relative to the worktree merge preview, but the reviewer had correctly observed that the server’s landing preflight had previously failed. Merging `main` was the appropriate way to bring the branch up to date and verify that integration no longer reports a conflict. The branch is now mergeable according to the current RepoOS landability output, although a fresh review lock is expected only after handoff.

An earlier task history includes failed handoffs caused by an absent engineering report draft and a prior timeout. This turn supplies the required draft before requesting review. No human device, account, or external system access was needed for the acceptance criteria.

## Key learnings

Recency is useful only when it distinguishes a healthy task from a quiet one. Keeping it on every healthy status line makes the most common state longer while giving little new information. The status label should carry state; the tooltip can carry precise timing; the inline line should reserve age for silent or stuck cases.

The board and pipeline presentations derive related but distinct details, so their presentation decisions belong at their UI boundaries while formatting belongs in a small shared helper. Tests should exercise both the rendered labels and the interaction path, especially touch, where a tooltip trigger can otherwise be mistaken for the card’s primary action.

Finally, a reported merge conflict needs validation against the current integration state. The local preview identified no overlapping content conflict, and a real merge confirmed that the task branch could incorporate `main` without changing the feature code. RepoOS landability then provided independent confirmation that the merge blocker was gone.
